reductionDefinition:
This reduction converts an independent set problem into a clique problem, 
                                            by taking the complement of the graph, or inverting all the edges.

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: In a graph G = (V, E), an independent set is a subset X of vertices no two of which are adjacent
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: An Independent Set is a set of nodes in a graph G, where no node is connected to another node in the set
reductionFrom.inputDescription: G, a graph, and K, the size of the independent set
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether G has an independent set of size K
reductionFrom.source: Wikimedia Foundation. (2025, September 8). Independent set (graph theory). Wikipedia.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {((N,E),K) | N is set, E subset N unorderedcross N, K is int} Example: (({a,b,c,d,e,f,g},{{a,b},{b,c},{c,a},{a,d},{d,e},{e,a},{f,e},{f,d},{g,b},{g,a}}),3)
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: independent set of exactly K node names | no two joined by an edge in E Example: {c,d,g}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Independent Set problem

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Clique = {<G, k> | G is an graph that has a set of k mutually adjacent nodes}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: A clique is the problem of uncovering a subset of vertices in an undirected graph G = (V, E) such that every two distinct vertices are adjacent
reductionTo.inputDescription: G, a graph, and k, the size of clique to find
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether G contains a clique of size k
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Clique problem

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Clique
